newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Arthuis calls Socialist job claims "lies".
newsitem.headline: France's Arthuis calls Socialist job claims "lies".

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis dismissed as "lies" a Socialist Party leader's insistence that trimming the working week to 35 hours from 39 would create 700,000 to 800,000 jobs.
"If lowering the working week by four hours would create 700,000 to 800,000 jobs, lowering it by 19 hours would create more than three million," Arthuis said in a statement.
"The Socialist Party should know that the French people do not believe these lies," he said.

Arthuis was responding to remarks by ex-prime minister Michel Rocard, who reiterated in an interview on Europe 1 radio that the Socialists wanted to create jobs by shrinking the working week without reducing pay.
The comments were made two weeks before the first round of France's May 25-June 1 parliamentary election.

Arthuis said labour costs would increase by 11 percent in both the private and public sectors should the working week be cut and said the Socialists had not spelled out how the extra costs would be paid for.
